- *→ continues at* [c1r](#dlg-inquiry-c1r)

<a id="dlg-inquiry-c1r"></a>`c1r` **MARTA**: The charge is that she was lost, Fenn. Show me she wasn't. <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:29</sub>
- **1.** **FENN**: (Show Ansel's log.) <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:30</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [c1ok](#dlg-inquiry-c1ok) *(above)*
- **2.** **FENN**: (Show the harbour ledger.) *[if has harbour ledger]* <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:31</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [c1_ledger](#dlg-inquiry-c1_ledger) *(above)*
- **3.** **FENN**: (Show the claims book.) *[if has claims book]* <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:32</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [c1_claims_book](#dlg-inquiry-c1_claims_book)
- **4.** **FENN**: (Show Rook's purse.) *[if has Rook's purse]* <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:33</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [c1_purse](#dlg-inquiry-c1_purse)
- **5.** **FENN**: (Show the kelp manifest.) *[if has kelp manifest]* <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:34</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [c1_kelp](#dlg-inquiry-c1_kelp)

<a id="dlg-inquiry-c1_claims_book"></a>`c1_claims_book` **SILAS CRAY**: My insurers paid out on a lost ship. That rather supports her being lost, doesn't it? Do keep helping. I'm enjoying it. <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:37</sub>
- *→ continues at* [c1r](#dlg-inquiry-c1r) *(above)*

<a id="dlg-inquiry-c1_purse"></a>`c1_purse` **OLD ROOK**: Not yet, boy. I'll know when it's my turn. I'll be the one standing up. <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:39</sub>
- *→ continues at* [c1r](#dlg-inquiry-c1r) *(above)*

<a id="dlg-inquiry-c1_kelp"></a>`c1_kelp` **MARTA**: Put that away, Fenn. I can smell it from here, and I've a feeling it's for afters. <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:41</sub>
- *→ continues at* [c1r](#dlg-inquiry-c1r) *(above)*

<a id="dlg-inquiry-enjoy"></a>`enjoy` **SILAS CRAY**: Oh, I shall. It's on the harbour's account, and tonight I'm the harbour. <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:6</sub>
- *[ends]*

*[entry points opened directly from elsewhere, or reached only from them:]*

*[waiting: opened directly from rooms/tavern.adv:153]*

<a id="dlg-inquiry-waiting"></a>`waiting` **SILAS CRAY**: I'm waiting for my escort, clerk. They're finishing their drinks. I told them not to hurry; I'd hate to be rushed out of my own ruin. <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:177</sub>
- *[sets cray_gone]* <sub>dialogue/inquiry.adv:178</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-ledger4"></a>
### Conversation: ledger4 (Marta)

*[source:* `dialogue ledger4`*, starts at* `open`*]* <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:2</sub>

<a id="dlg-ledger4-open"></a>`open` **FENN (V.O.)**: I open the harbour ledger on the bar, at the page I walked past for three years without once turning to it. ARCADIA. LOST AT SEA. In Bramwick's hand, three days early. <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:3</sub>
- *→ continues at* [quiet](#dlg-ledger4-quiet)

<a id="dlg-ledger4-quiet"></a>`quiet` **FENN (V.O.)**: The room goes quiet. Bramwick takes his hat off. Rook takes his off too, finds he isn't wearing one, and holds his mug to his chest instead. <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:5</sub>
- **1.** **FENN**: (Write.) <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:6</sub>
  - *[sets ledger_written]* <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:7</sub>
  - *[casebook:* I wrote it all into the harbour ledger and signed my name under it, which is either the bravest or the most clerical thing I have ever done.*]* <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:8</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [write](#dlg-ledger4-write)

<a id="dlg-ledger4-write"></a>`write` **FENN (V.O.)**: Underneath, in my best customs hand, I write: ARCADIA: returned. All hands. <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:9</sub>
- *→ continues at* [stamp](#dlg-ledger4-stamp)

<a id="dlg-ledger4-stamp"></a>`stamp` **FENN (V.O.)**: Then I stamp it. The stamp comes down on the page like a door closing behind somebody who has come home. <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:11</sub>
- *[sound: chime]* <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:12</sub>
- *→ continues at* [ending](#dlg-ledger4-ending)

<a id="dlg-ledger4-ending"></a>`ending` **MARTA**: Now that's an ending. <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:14</sub>
- **1.** **FENN**: Not quite. There's a ship sailing at dawn. <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:15</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [dawn](#dlg-ledger4-dawn)
- **2.** **FENN**: (Close the book.) <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:16</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [closed](#dlg-ledger4-closed)

<a id="dlg-ledger4-dawn"></a>`dawn` **MARTA**: Then go and catch it, you daft article. Or don't. But go and say so to her face. <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:17</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-ledger4-closed"></a>`closed` **FENN (V.O.)**: I close the book. For the first time in three years I don't know what the next page says, and I find I like it. <sub>dialogue/ledger4.adv:18</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="act4-alley"></a>
## Chandler's Lane

*[room* `alley`*; also in Act I; lines for every act are under Act I]* <sub>rooms/alley.adv:1</sub>

**Cray & Co.** `counting_door` *[present Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/alley.adv:77</sub>

- **Look at:** Further up the lane, past where Cray used to stand and wait for me: a brass plate, a polished door, a little cloud. CRAY & CO., FACTORS. There's a light on. <sub>rooms/alley.adv:82</sub>
- **Use / Walk to:** *[→ goes to Cray & Co., Factors]* <sub>rooms/alley.adv:81</sub>
- **Open:** I go up the lane to Cray & Co. The brass plate has been polished so hard it's nearly gone. <sub>rooms/alley.adv:83</sub>
  - *[→ goes to Cray & Co., Factors]* <sub>rooms/alley.adv:81</sub>

<a id="act4-pier_end"></a>
## The Pier End

*[room* `pier_end`*]* <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:2</sub>

**back along the pier** `town` <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:16</sub>

- **Look at:** Back along the pier, the lights of Port Vela, and somewhere among them the Salty Keel, singing. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:20</sub>
- **Use / Open / Walk to:** *[→ goes to Vela Docks]* <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:19</sub>

**Cray's cutter** `cutter` <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:22</sub>

- **Look at:** A grey cutter with a cloud on her furled sail: the one that ran out of the lagoon ahead of us. Fast, neat, and built for getting home first, which is the whole of Cray's business. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:25</sub>
- **Talk to:** I say something cutting to the cutter. It's the best I can do at this hour. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:27</sub>
- **Open:** There's nothing aboard but the smell of kelp and the feeling of being watched by a gangplank. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:26</sub>

**Weather man** `wilf` *[present if inquiry_done = false]* <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:29</sub>

- **Look at:** One of Cray's men, grey coat, yellow armband, carrying a crate of kelp to the cart as if it were a sleeping child. He is very polite and very large. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:33</sub>
- **Talk to:** He sets the crate down on the cart and touches his hat. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:34</sub>
  - *[→ conversation* [weather4](#dlg-weather4) *— below]* <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:35</sub>
- **Give:** “Can't take anything without a docket, sir. Mr Cray's very strict.” <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:36</sub>

**Weather man** `bartle` *[present if inquiry_done = false]* <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:38</sub>

- **Look at:** Another of Cray's men, by the lamp, holding a crate and a grudge. The grudge is about whose turn it is. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:42</sub>
- **Talk to:** He nods at his colleague. “Talk to Wilf, sir. Wilf's on menacing.” <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:43</sub>
  - *[→ conversation* [weather4](#dlg-weather4) *— below]* <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:44</sub>
- **Give:** “Docket first, sir.” <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:45</sub>

**kelp crates** `crates` <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:47</sub>

- **Look at:** Crates stencilled QUARANTINE STN, G.K., with a little cloud painted over the stencil, badly, which is how you know the stencil mattered. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:50</sub>
- **Open:** Nailed shut, and two large men are standing next to them, being polite in my direction. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:51</sub>
- *When* *[if kelp_seen]* <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:52</sub>
  - **Look at:** The same crates as on the Marrow's deck: QUARANTINE STN, G.K., with a cloud painted over it. I've seen what's inside. It burns like a lie. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:53</sub>

**manifest on the crate** `kelp_manifest` *[present if doesn't have kelp manifest and kelp_proof = false]* *[Pick up gives: kelp manifest]* <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:55</sub>

- **Look at:** A manifest, tacked to the top crate for whoever signs for it. Nobody's signing for it. They're too busy deciding whose turn it is to be menacing. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:60</sub>
- **Pick up:** While they argue about whose turn it is to be menacing, I lift the manifest off the crate. I'm customs. Manifests come to me the way cats come to people who don't want cats. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:61</sub>
  - *[sets kelp_proof]* <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:62</sub>

**stacked crates** `stack` <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:64</sub>

- **Look at:** More of Cray's kelp, stacked for the cart, sacked and stencilled. Enough fog for a month of Tuesdays. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:67</sub>

**the lighthouse** `lighthouse` <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:69</sub>

- **Look at:** The Vela light, turning over the harbour mouth. Three years I watched ships leave by it. Last night I came home by it. It looks smaller from the sea, which I'm told is the point. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:72</sub>

**the harbour mouth** `sea` <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:74</sub>

- **Look at:** The harbour mouth, black and moving, and past it the Straits. They don't look any different. I am, I think. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:77</sub>

**Combinations here**

- **Use crowbar on kelp crates:** *[if kelp_seen]* I've already seen inside one of these, on the Marrow. Once was plenty. Kelp smells exactly like a lie on fire. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:80</sub>
- **Use crowbar on kelp crates:** One of the Weather men clears his throat, politely, and shifts a crate to his other arm, so his hand is free. I put the crowbar away. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:82</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on Weather man:** “Customs, Wilf,” says one. “Told you,” says the other. Neither of them stops unloading. <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:84</sub>
- **Use kelp manifest on Weather man:** “You keep that, sir. It's only kelp.” He thinks about it. “Don't keep it too hard.” <sub>rooms/pier_end.adv:86</sub>

<a id="dlg-weather4"></a>
### Conversation: weather4 (A Weather man, Another Weather man)

*[source:* `dialogue weather4`*, starts at* `root`*]* <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:2</sub>

<a id="dlg-weather4-root"></a>`root` **A WEATHER MAN**: Evening, sir. We're unloading. Nothing to see. It's kelp. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:3</sub>
- **1.** **FENN**: What's the kelp for? *[if seen:weather4.for = false]* <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:4</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [for](#dlg-weather4-for)
- **2.** **FENN**: Aren't you meant to be menacing me? *[if seen:weather4.menace = false]* <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:5</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [menace](#dlg-weather4-menace)
- **3.** **FENN**: Who signs for it? *[if seen:weather4.signs = false]* <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:6</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [signs](#dlg-weather4-signs)
- **4.** **FENN**: I've seen kelp crates like those before. On the Marrow. *[if kelp_seen and seen:weather4.marrow = false]* <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:7</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [marrow](#dlg-weather4-marrow)
- **5.** **FENN**: Goodnight. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:8</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [bye](#dlg-weather4-bye)

<a id="dlg-weather4-for"></a>`for` **A WEATHER MAN**: Fog. — <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:9</sub>
- *→ continues at* [fires](#dlg-weather4-fires)

<a id="dlg-weather4-fires"></a>`fires` **ANOTHER WEATHER MAN**: Fires! It's for fires, sir. Fog's just what fires do if you're not careful. We're very careful. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:11</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-weather4-menace"></a>`menace` **A WEATHER MAN**: Not my turn, sir. It's Bartle's turn. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:12</sub>
- *→ continues at* [tuesday](#dlg-weather4-tuesday)

<a id="dlg-weather4-tuesday"></a>`tuesday` **ANOTHER WEATHER MAN**: I did Tuesday. I did all last week. My voice is shot from menacing. You do him. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:14</sub>
- *→ continues at* [argue](#dlg-weather4-argue)

<a id="dlg-weather4-argue"></a>`argue` **FENN (V.O.)**: They argue about it, politely, with their backs to the crates. Nobody menaces me at all. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:16</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-weather4-signs"></a>`signs` **A WEATHER MAN**: Mr Cray, sir. Everything's signed for. There's a manifest on the crate, if you're customs. You're not customs? <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:17</sub>
- *→ continues at* [customs](#dlg-weather4-customs)

<a id="dlg-weather4-customs"></a>`customs` **ANOTHER WEATHER MAN**: He's got a stamp, Wilf. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:19</sub>
- *→ continues at* [dont](#dlg-weather4-dont)

<a id="dlg-weather4-dont"></a>`dont` **A WEATHER MAN**: Then don't look at it too hard, sir. It's only kelp. It's shy. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:21</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-weather4-marrow"></a>`marrow` **A WEATHER MAN**: The Marrow? Can't be, sir. Them crates were for the station. Station's shut, they tell us. Nobody's told the kelp. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:22</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-weather4-bye"></a>`bye` **A WEATHER MAN**: Goodnight, sir. Mind the fog. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:23</sub>
- *→ continues at* [nofog](#dlg-weather4-nofog)

<a id="dlg-weather4-nofog"></a>`nofog` **ANOTHER WEATHER MAN**: There isn't any fog. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:25</sub>
- *→ continues at* [anyway](#dlg-weather4-anyway)

<a id="dlg-weather4-anyway"></a>`anyway` **A WEATHER MAN**: Mind it anyway. <sub>dialogue/weather4.adv:27</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="act4-village"></a>
## Upper Town

*[room* `village`*; also in Act I; lines for every act are under Act I]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:2</sub>

**Nell** `nell` <sub>rooms/village.adv:20</sub>

- *When* *[Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:28</sub>
  - **Look at:** Nell, at her stall, selling rope to nobody and gossip to everybody. Tonight the gossip is true, and it has her rattled. <sub>rooms/village.adv:29</sub>
  - **Talk to:** She waves me over with a dried fish. <sub>rooms/village.adv:30</sub>
    - *[→ conversation* [nell at news](#dlg-nell-news) *— see Act I › Upper Town]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:31</sub>

**Tam** `tam` <sub>rooms/village.adv:33</sub>

- *When* *[Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:41</sub>
  - **Look at:** Tam, on the wall, with his cap pushed back, counting people up the steps. He has run out of slate and started on the wall. <sub>rooms/village.adv:42</sub>
  - **Talk to:** He holds up a finger without looking round. “Hang on. A hundred and twelve. Go on.” <sub>rooms/village.adv:43</sub>
    - *[→ conversation* [tam at home](#dlg-tam-home) *— see Act I › Upper Town]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:44</sub>

**Old Onn** `onn` <sub>rooms/village.adv:46</sub>

- *When* *[Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:54</sub>
  - **Look at:** Old Onn, on her clean step, with the broom across her knees. She isn't sweeping. She's waiting, and she's seen me. <sub>rooms/village.adv:55</sub>
  - **Talk to:** She puts the broom down before I've said a word. <sub>rooms/village.adv:56</sub>
    - *[→ conversation* [onn at home](#dlg-onn-home) *— see Act I › Upper Town]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:57</sub>

**Tam Hobb** `tamhobb` *[present Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:59</sub>

- **Look at:** Tam Hobb, home, salt still in his beard, standing beside his son as if he's been told not to move until he's been counted. He has brought his rake. Nobody has had the heart to mention it. <sub>rooms/village.adv:63</sub>
- **Talk to:** He leans on the rake out of habit, then remembers there's no salt. <sub>rooms/village.adv:64</sub>
  - *[→ conversation* [tamhobb at home](#dlg-tamhobb-home) *— see Act III › Gullet Key — the Salt Camp]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:65</sub>
- **Give:** “I've got everything I want, clerk. It's mostly standing on this street.” <sub>rooms/village.adv:66</sub>

**washing line** `washing` <sub>rooms/village.adv:90</sub>

- *When* *[Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:94</sub>
  - **Look at:** The washing line. Nine shirts, and a tenth, pegged up still dripping, big enough to sail a dinghy. Somebody on this street is washing for a man who came home. <sub>rooms/village.adv:95</sub>

**the houses** `cottages` <sub>rooms/village.adv:97</sub>

- *When* *[Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/village.adv:101</sub>
  - **Look at:** Every window on the street is lit. A door has been left open, and from inside somebody is laughing too loudly to be anything but relieved. <sub>rooms/village.adv:102</sub>

<a id="act4-chandlery"></a>
## The Chandler's

*[room* `chandlery`*; also in Act I; lines for every act are under Act I]* <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:1</sub>

**the counter** `counter` <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:11</sub>

- *When* *[Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:17</sub>
  - **Look at:** The counter. Every invoice on the spike is stamped PAID now. Mr Tallow has framed the first one and hung it over the till. <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:18</sub>

**back room** `back_room` <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:28</sub>

- *When* *[Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:36</sub>
  - **Look at:** The back room is dark. A note on the door, in Mr Tallow's harassed capitals: GONE TO THE KEEL. CAT IN CHARGE. <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:37</sub>
  - **Talk to:** Nobody answers. Mr Tallow has gone to the Keel, and the cat has gone with him, in charge. <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:38</sub>
    - *[nothing: cancels the usual effects]*
  - **Open:** It's his back room. Even with the cat out, I'm not that sort of clerk. <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:40</sub>

**Combinations here**

- **Use harbour stamp on the counter:** *[Act IV only]* Everything's paid. Stamping it again would just be showing off, and Mr Tallow isn't here to see. <sub>rooms/chandlery.adv:49</sub>

<a id="act4-warehouse"></a>
## Harbour Loft

*[room* `warehouse`*; also in Act I; lines for every act are under Act I]* <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:1</sub>

**harbour ledger** `ledger` *[present if ledger_taken = false]* <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:13</sub>

- *When* *[Act IV only]* <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:26</sub>
  - **Look at:** The harbour ledger, still chained to its desk. The Arcadia's entry is where I left it: lost at sea, three days early, paid for by Cray & Co. <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:27</sub>
  - **Use:** I've read it. Reading it won't be enough; Cray's counting on that. The inquiry will want the book itself, and the book is chained to the desk. <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:30</sub>
    - *[nothing: cancels the usual effects]*
  - **Open:** I've read it. Reading it won't be enough; Cray's counting on that. The inquiry will want the book itself, and the book is chained to the desk. <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:28</sub>
    - *[nothing: cancels the usual effects]*
  - **Pull:** Chained. Bramwick chained it there himself, by regulation, so it could never go anywhere it might be embarrassed. <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:32</sub>
  - **Pick up:** It's chained to the desk. Regulation thirty-one, and a very good padlock. <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:33</sub>

**broken chain** `chain` *[present Act IV, if ledger_taken]* <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:49</sub>

- **Look at:** A broken chain, and a clean oblong in the dust where the ledger sat for thirty years. Regulation thirty-one has been suspended, like its author. <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:53</sub>

**Combinations here**

- **Use crowbar on harbour ledger:** *[Act IV only]* I get the crowbar through the chain where it meets the desk, and lean. The staple comes out of thirty years of oak with a noise like a held breath let go. The ledger is mine to carry. <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:56</sub>
  - *[Fenn receives: harbour ledger]* *[sets ledger_taken]* *[sound: pickup]* <sub>rooms/warehouse.adv:57</sub>

<a id="act4-counting_house"></a>
## Cray & Co., Factors

*[room* `counting_house`*]* <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:2</sub>

**the counting desks** `desks` <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:12</sub>

- **Look at:** Five tall desks in a row, every pen lined up with the one beside it. Even the ink looks like it's been told to sit up straight. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:15</sub>
- **Open:** Locked, every drawer. The keys will be on a ring in Cray's pocket, alphabetised. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:16</sub>

**the pigeonholes** `pigeonholes` <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:18</sub>

- **Look at:** Hundreds of pigeonholes, numbered, each with a rolled paper in it. Bills of lading, salvage receipts, insurance. A whole wall of other people's bad luck, filed. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:21</sub>
- **Pick up:** I reach for one, and Nib clears his throat without looking up. It's the most alarming noise I've heard all night. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:22</sub>

**portrait of Silas Cray** `portrait` <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:24</sub>

- **Look at:** Silas Cray, in oils, looking down at his own office the way he looks at everything: as if he's already insured it against you. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:27</sub>
- **Talk to:** I tell the portrait that it's going to have a very long morning. The portrait smirks. It was painted smirking. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:28</sub>

**brass cloud** `emblem` <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:30</sub>

- **Look at:** The Cray & Co. cloud, in polished brass. The same cloud that was painted on the kelp crates, and pressed in wax on Rook's purse. A cloud is a fine mark for a man who sells fog. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:33</sub>

**the safe** `safe` <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:35</sub>

- **Look at:** A black iron safe with a brass dial. Whatever's in there is the part Cray thought was worth hiding. Everything he thought was harmless, he left on the shelves. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:38</sub>
- **Use:** I don't know the combination, and I'm not the sort of clerk who guesses. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:40</sub>
- **Open:** I don't know the combination, and I'm not the sort of clerk who guesses. The interesting books are never in the safe anyway. They're in the pigeonholes, being boring. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:39</sub>

**requisition tray** `tray` *[present if doesn't have requisition and doesn't have claims book and inquiry_done = false]* *[Pick up gives: requisition]* <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:42</sub>

- **Look at:** An in-tray of blank requisitions, on Nib's desk. CRAY & CO. REQUISITION: ITEM, QUANTITY, AUTHORITY. Each with a little cloud at the top, smiling. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:47</sub>
- **Pick up:** I take a requisition and fill it in on the desk, in my neatest hand: one claims book, insurance, all of it. Authorised: Harbour of Port Vela. Nib doesn't look up. He was right; he doesn't read anything. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:48</sub>

**Nib** `nib` <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:50</sub>

- **Look at:** Cray's clerk: a young man in an eyeshade, with ink to the elbows and the expression of somebody waiting for a clock to tell him he can stop. The clock hasn't. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:53</sub>
- **Talk to:** He looks up from nothing in particular. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:54</sub>
  - *[→ conversation* [nib](#dlg-nib) *— below]* <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:55</sub>
- **Give:** “I can't take things. I can only take requisitions.” <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:56</sub>
- *When* *[if has claims book]* <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:57</sub>
  - **Talk to:** *[→ conversation* [nib at after](#dlg-nib-after) *— below]* <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:58</sub>

**door to the lane** `door_out` <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:60</sub>

- **Look at:** The door back out to Chandler's Lane. Polished on the inside too. Nobody polishes the inside of a door. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:64</sub>
- **Use / Open / Walk to:** *[→ goes to Chandler's Lane]* <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:63</sub>

**Combinations here**

- **Use requisition on Nib:** *[if req_stamped]* I hand Nib the requisition. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:67</sub>
  - *[Fenn hands over: requisition]* *[Fenn receives: claims book]* *[sound: chime]* *[→ conversation* [nib at handed](#dlg-nib-handed) *— below]* <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:68</sub>
- **Use requisition on Nib:** He turns it over, looking for something, and hands it back. “It isn't stamped. I can't not read it if it isn't stamped.” <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:73</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on Nib:** He holds out the back of his hand, considers it, and withdraws it. “No. Then I'd be authorised. I don't know what I'd do.” <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:75</sub>
- **Use brass compass on Nib:** “It's pointing at the wall.” It is. Past the wall is the reef. He doesn't ask. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:77</sub>
- **Use harbour ledger on Nib:** “That's the harbour's. We don't keep the harbour's. We just pay it.” He hears himself, and frowns, faintly. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:79</sub>
- **Use crowbar on the safe:** I measure the crowbar against the safe. The safe wins on every measurement, including morally. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:81</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on the pigeonholes:** Stamping Cray's own filing would be very satisfying and of no use whatsoever. I'll stamp something that counts. <sub>rooms/counting_house.adv:83</sub>

<a id="dlg-nib"></a>
### Conversation: nib (Nib)

*[source:* `dialogue nib`*, starts at* `root`*]* <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:2</sub>

<a id="dlg-nib-root"></a>`root` **NIB**: Cray and Company. Closed. I'm only here because nobody told me to go home. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:3</sub>
- **1.** **FENN**: What's in all those books? *[if seen:nib.books = false]* <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:4</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [books](#dlg-nib-books)
- **2.** **FENN**: I'd like your insurance claims book. *[if doesn't have claims book]* <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:5</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [claims](#dlg-nib-claims)
- **3.** **FENN**: How long have you worked here? *[if seen:nib.long = false]* <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:6</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [long](#dlg-nib-long)
- **4.** **FENN**: Go home, Nib. *[if seen:nib.home = false]* <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:7</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [home](#dlg-nib-home)
- **5.** **FENN**: Goodnight. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:8</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [bye](#dlg-nib-bye)

<a id="dlg-nib-books"></a>`books` **NIB**: No idea. I don't read them. Nobody reads them. That's what they're for. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:9</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-nib-claims"></a>`claims` **NIB**: I can't give you things. I can only give things to requisitions. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:10</sub>
- *→ continues at* [claims2](#dlg-nib-claims2)

<a id="dlg-nib-claims2"></a>`claims2` **NIB**: Requisitions are in the tray. They have to be stamped. I don't read them. I look for the stamp. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:12</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-nib-long"></a>`long` **NIB**: Three years. I started the week the Arcadia went. Mr Cray said he needed somebody who never reads anything. I'm the best he's ever had. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:13</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-nib-home"></a>`home` **NIB**: Is that an instruction? <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:14</sub>
- **1.** **FENN**: It's a kindness. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:15</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [kind](#dlg-nib-kind)
- **2.** **FENN**: I used to be a clerk. I read everything. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:16</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [everything](#dlg-nib-everything)

<a id="dlg-nib-kind"></a>`kind` **NIB**: We don't have those here. …Could you put it on a form? <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:17</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-nib-everything"></a>`everything` **NIB**: (horrified) Everything? Even the backs? <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:18</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-nib-bye"></a>`bye` **NIB**: Is it? I hadn't looked. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:19</sub>
- *[ends]*

*[handed: opened directly from rooms/counting_house.adv:71]*

<a id="dlg-nib-handed"></a>`handed` **FENN (V.O.)**: Nib looks at the stamp, not the words. He takes a fat ledger from pigeonhole one, dusts it with his sleeve, and hands it over without opening it. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:21</sub>
- *→ continues at* [nice](#dlg-nib-nice)

<a id="dlg-nib-nice"></a>`nice` **NIB**: Stamped. Have a nice night. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:23</sub>
- **1.** **FENN**: Do you know what you've just given me? <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:24</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [know](#dlg-nib-know)
- **2.** **FENN**: Thank you, Nib. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:25</sub>
  - *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-nib-know"></a>`know` **NIB**: A book. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:26</sub>
- *→ continues at* [ruin](#dlg-nib-ruin)

<a id="dlg-nib-ruin"></a>`ruin` **FENN**: Your employer's ruin, more or less. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:28</sub>
- **1.** **FENN**: … <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:29</sub>
  - *→ continues at* [stamped](#dlg-nib-stamped)

<a id="dlg-nib-stamped"></a>`stamped` **NIB**: Was it stamped? Then it's not my problem. It's the stamp's. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:30</sub>
- *[ends]*

<a id="dlg-nib-after"></a>`after` **NIB**: Got another requisition? I like them. They tell you what to do, and then you've done it. <sub>dialogue/nib.adv:31</sub>

<a id="global-combos"></a>
# Combinations that work anywhere

*[from combos.adv: these apply in every room, after the room's own combinations]*

- **Use harbour stamp on licence form:** I stamp the form as a clerk of this house, in the Harbourmaster's legal absence. It now says I'm fit to sail, in a font nobody can argue with. <sub>combos.adv:8</sub>
  - *[Fenn hands over: licence form]* *[Fenn receives: stamped licence]* <sub>combos.adv:9</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on Bill of Health:** *[if bill_stamped = false]* I stamp the Bill of Health: HARBOUR OF PORT VELA, in purple, slightly crooked, which is how you know it's real. <sub>combos.adv:14</sub>
  - *[sets bill_stamped]* *[sound: chime]* <sub>combos.adv:15</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on Bill of Health:** It's stamped. Stamping it twice would look desperate, and Pike can smell desperate. <sub>combos.adv:19</sub>
- **Use calendar leaf on Bill of Health:** I copy today's date onto the bill in my neatest figures, and pin the leaf behind it as a receipt. Dated. Nobody ever does the dating. <sub>combos.adv:22</sub>
  - *[Fenn hands over: calendar leaf]* *[sets bill_dated]* *[sound: chime]* <sub>combos.adv:23</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on requisition:** *[if req_stamped = false]* Any clerk of this house may stamp in the Harbourmaster's absence. Tonight the Harbourmaster is very absent. I stamp the requisition: HARBOUR OF PORT VELA, square in the middle of Cray's little cloud. <sub>combos.adv:29</sub>
  - *[sets req_stamped]* *[sound: chime]* <sub>combos.adv:30</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on requisition:** It's stamped. Nib only looks for one. Two would make him nervous, and then he might read it. <sub>combos.adv:34</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on harbour ledger:** *[if quarantine_lifted = false]* Not yet. Until Marta says otherwise, this book is evidence, and you don't stamp evidence. You hold it up. <sub>combos.adv:38</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on harbour ledger:** *[if ledger_written = false]* Not here. An entry like this one wants witnesses, and the Salty Keel is full of them. <sub>combos.adv:41</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on harbour ledger:** It's stamped. Once is a correction. Twice is a nervous habit. <sub>combos.adv:44</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on stamped licence:** It's stamped. A second stamp would make it look nervous, and a nervous licence gets read. <sub>combos.adv:81</sub>
- **Use harbour stamp on manifest copy:** Stamping it would make it a customs document, and then it would belong to the harbour. It belongs to twenty-two other people. <sub>combos.adv:84</sub>

<a id="items"></a>
# Items

**crowbar** `crowbar` — A crowbar with ambitions well beyond leaning on bollards. <sub>items.adv:4</sub>

**jet-caps** `mushroom` — Jet-caps. Black-capped, wet, and worth more than they look. They grow in timber the fog has been at, and Marta will not serve her broth without them. <sub>items.adv:7</sub>

**licence form** `licence_form` — A blank Seafarer's Licence. Name, rank, and a box marked “previous piracy, if any”. Worthless until it carries the harbour stamp. <sub>items.adv:10</sub>

**drawer key** `drawer_key` — Bramwick's drawer key. Lost at cards, traded for a handful of mushrooms. A distinguished career, for a key. <sub>items.adv:13</sub>

**harbour stamp** `stamp` — The harbour stamp. Brass, heavy, and far more powerful than it looks. <sub>items.adv:16</sub>

**stamped licence** `licence` — My Seafarer's Licence, stamped by a clerk of the customs house in the Harbourmaster's legal absence. The ink is still wet. <sub>items.adv:19</sub>

**brass compass** `compass` — My father's compass. My grandfather made it, my father sailed by it, and then one morning he left it on the hall table and sailed without it. It has never once pointed north. <sub>items.adv:22</sub>

- *[Act I, if has stamped licence and has manifest copy and ledger_read]* The needle points at the customs house like a dog that's found something. Bramwick, then. With everything. <sub>items.adv:24</sub>
- *[Act I, if has stamped licence and ledger_read = false]* The needle leans toward the lane. The harbour ledger is up in the loft over the chandler's. <sub>items.adv:26</sub>
- *[Act I, if has stamped licence and doesn't have manifest copy]* Bramwick wants the Arcadia's manifest copy. The chandler keeps one, if somebody settles his invoices. <sub>items.adv:28</sub>
- *[Act I, if has harbour stamp and doesn't have stamped licence]* A harbour stamp and a clerk who knows where the licence forms are. Even the needle can see where this is going. <sub>items.adv:30</sub>
- *[Act I, if has drawer key]* Bramwick's drawer key. The needle points at the customs house, or at least doesn't object to it. <sub>items.adv:32</sub>
- *[Act I, if has jet-caps]* Someone in Port Vela wants what grows under the pier. The needle swings toward the tavern, and waits. <sub>items.adv:34</sub>
- *[Act I, if knows_key]* Marta has the drawer key and wants jet-caps. They come up under the stacked crate on the pier. <sub>items.adv:36</sub>
- *[Act I only]* My father's compass. It has never once pointed north. Tonight it leans toward the customs house: Bramwick will know how a clerk gets a licence. <sub>items.adv:38</sub>
- *[Act II, if vane_convinced]* The needle has stopped pretending to be a compass. It points over the bow, into the fog, at a reef nobody sails. Forward, then. <sub>items.adv:40</sub>
- *[Act II, if quill_navigator and crew_agree]* A navigator, a crew, and Pell's last sentence in my pocket. The needle points aft, at the captain's cabin, and waits. <sub>items.adv:42</sub>
- *[Act II, if has Pell's sextant and vane_terms]* Pell's sextant. The needle swings toward the one person on board who wants to be a navigator more than she wants breakfast. <sub>items.adv:44</sub>
- *[Act II, if vane_terms and dinner and chest_open = false]* Hobb has gone to his dinner. The needle points below decks, at a sea-chest nobody opens. <sub>items.adv:46</sub>
- *[Act II, if vane_terms and dinner and crew_agree = false]* Hobb won't sail south for money, only for blood. I'm carrying a list of twenty-two names. The needle has opinions about that. <sub>items.adv:48</sub>
- *[Act II, if vane_terms and dinner = false]* Three terms, and a bosun sitting on Pell's chest until dinner. The needle points below decks, toward a cook without a stamp. <sub>items.adv:50</sub>
- *[Act II, if quill_helped]* The needle wants the captain's cabin. Down the companionway at the stern, and onto her chart. <sub>items.adv:52</sub>
- *[Act II, if has spyglass]* Quill's spyglass. She wants it back, and I want to get past her. Commerce. <sub>items.adv:54</sub>
- *[Act II only]* The needle points aft, past the lookout. Quill won't let a clerk by unless he's useful. <sub>items.adv:56</sub>
- *[Act III, if has flag sixteen]* The needle points back across the flats at the wreck and her halyard, like a dog that wants to be let out. Sixteen, then. Up. <sub>items.adv:58</sub>
- *[Act III, if quill_free]* My father, in a salt pan, with a flag under his arm. For once the needle has nothing to add. Talk to him. <sub>items.adv:60</sub>
- *[Act III, if form9]* Form 9, written out clean and stamped. The needle points at Pike, who is going to love it. Then hate it. Then love it. <sub>items.adv:62</sub>
- *[Act III, if knows_form9]* There isn't a Form 9 on all of Gullet Key. There's a clerk with a harbour stamp and the blank back of a Bill of Health. <sub>items.adv:64</sub>
- *[Act III, if fog_down]* Quill is locked in the store hut, pending inspection. The needle points at Pike. Somebody here knows what form lets a person out. <sub>items.adv:66</sub>
- *[Act III, if gate_open and has bucket of lagoon]* A bucket of lagoon, and a brazier making all the fog. The needle points at the Weather Works with a certain relish. <sub>items.adv:68</sub>
- *[Act III, if gate_open and has bucket]* The great brazier at the Weather Works is making the fog. My bucket is empty. The lagoon isn't. <sub>items.adv:70</sub>
- *[Act III, if gate_open]* The great brazier is making the fog, and fire hates water. There was a bucket in my father's cabin. <sub>items.adv:72</sub>
- *[Act III, if has Bill of Health and bill_smoked and bill_stamped and bill_signed and bill_dated]* Fumigated, stamped, countersigned and dated. The needle swings toward Pike, practically wagging. <sub>items.adv:74</sub>
- *[Act III, if has calendar leaf]* A day, torn off Pike's calendar. The needle points at the Bill of Health, where days belong. <sub>items.adv:76</sub>
- *[Act III, if has Bill of Health and bill_smoked = false]* The bill smells of cupboard. Pike's fumigation brazier smoulders right beside his gate. <sub>items.adv:78</sub>
- *[Act III, if has Bill of Health and bill_stamped = false]* A Bill of Health without a harbour stamp. I happen to have a harbour stamp. The needle is embarrassed for me. <sub>items.adv:80</sub>
- *[Act III, if has Bill of Health and bill_signed = false]* It wants a ship's officer's countersignature. The needle swings toward the only navigator on the island. <sub>items.adv:82</sub>
- *[Act III, if has Bill of Health and bill_dated = false]* Undated. Pike's calendar is in his hut, and Pike can't take his eyes off it. Unless he's reciting something, eyes shut. <sub>items.adv:84</sub>
- *[Act III, if log_read]* Pike wants a Bill of Health. Every captain carries blanks; my father's are in the pigeonholes by his desk. <sub>items.adv:86</sub>
- *[Act III, if hatch_open]* The needle points down the hatch, at my father's desk. It's been waiting three years. So have I. <sub>items.adv:88</sub>
- *[Act III only]* The needle points at the Arcadia's deck hatch, which is jammed. Quill packed a crowbar. Of course she did. <sub>items.adv:90</sub>
- *[Act IV, if ledger_written]* The needle points down the pier, at a bollard with a navigator sitting on it. For once I don't need telling. <sub>items.adv:92</sub>
- *[Act IV, if quarantine_lifted and iou_paid = false]* A stamp, a ledger, and a page that's been wrong for three years. The needle points at the bar of the Salty Keel, though it keeps glancing at Bramwick, who keeps patting his coat pocket as if something in it might make a run for it. <sub>items.adv:94</sub>
- *[Act IV, if quarantine_lifted]* A stamp, a ledger, and a page that's been wrong for three years. The needle points at the bar of the Salty Keel. <sub>items.adv:96</sub>
- *[Act IV, if inquiry_done]* Bramwick is reinstated in everything but his stamp, which is in my pocket. The needle points at him, a little reproachfully. <sub>items.adv:98</sub>
- *[Act IV, if has harbour ledger and has Rook's purse and has claims book and kelp_proof = false]* Everything Bramwick asked for. The needle points at the Keel, where Cray is raising a glass. Then it twitches once toward the pier end, as if it's heard something about kelp. <sub>items.adv:100</sub>
- *[Act IV, if has harbour ledger and has Rook's purse and has claims book]* The ledger, the purse, the claims book, my father's log and a manifest that smells of fog. The needle points at the Salty Keel, and Cray. <sub>items.adv:102</sub>
- *[Act IV, if has requisition and req_stamped]* A stamped requisition. The needle points at Nib, who is going to enjoy not reading it. <sub>items.adv:104</sub>
- *[Act IV, if has requisition]* A requisition without a stamp. The needle looks at the pocket where the stamp is, and then at me. <sub>items.adv:106</sub>
- *[Act IV, if seen:nib.claims2 and doesn't have claims book]* Nib only answers to stamped requisitions, and there's a tray of blank ones on his desk. <sub>items.adv:108</sub>
- *[Act IV, if seen:bramwick4.paper and purse_given = false]* “A man who was there when it happened.” The needle swings toward the corner of the Keel, where Rook is pretending not to listen. <sub>items.adv:110</sub>
- *[Act IV, if seen:bramwick4.paper and ledger_taken = false]* The harbour ledger, chained to its desk in the loft. I have a crowbar. The needle has an opinion. <sub>items.adv:112</sub>
- *[Act IV, if seen:bramwick4.paper and doesn't have claims book]* Cray's insurance books live at Cray & Co., up Chandler's Lane. The needle points that way with distaste. <sub>items.adv:114</sub>
- *[Act IV, if farewell]* Cray has the chair, the ink and the dawn bell. The needle points at the Salty Keel, where a suspended harbourmaster is drinking. <sub>items.adv:116</sub>
- *[Act IV only]* The needle points out at the Marrow, at anchor past the boom. Quill is on the rail. <sub>items.adv:118</sub>

**spyglass** `spyglass` — A brass spyglass, dented twice and polished a thousand times. Somebody on this ship is squinting a lot this morning. <sub>items.adv:121</sub>

**Pell's sextant** `sextant` — Pell's sextant, polished to a mirror by forty years of thumbs. It measures the angle between a star and the sea, which is the kind of paperwork I can respect. <sub>items.adv:124</sub>

**Pell's log** `pell_log` — Pell's last entry: “If Ansel's boy ever comes aboard with the old man's compass, tell the captain she should”. Then nothing. Ansel's boy. That's me. I read it twice. <sub>items.adv:127</sub>

- *[if seen:vane.pell]* Pell's last entry: “If Ansel's boy ever comes aboard with the old man's compass, tell the captain she should”. Then nothing. He died mid-sentence. Vane said so. <sub>items.adv:129</sub>

**Bill of Health** `bill` — A Bill of Health. <sub>items.adv:132</sub>

- *[if form9]* Front: a Bill of Health, passed. Back: FORM 9, RELEASE OF DETAINED PERSONS, in my best hand. Both sides stamped. It's the best thing I've ever written. <sub>items.adv:134</sub>
- *[if gate_open]* The Arcadia's Bill of Health: fumigated, stamped, countersigned, dated and inspected. Pike made me promise to keep it on my person. The back is still blank. <sub>items.adv:136</sub>
- *[if bill_smoked and bill_stamped and bill_signed and bill_dated]* Fumigated, stamped, countersigned and dated. It's perfect. Pike is going to cry, and I may join him. <sub>items.adv:138</sub>
- *[if bill_smoked = false]* A Bill of Health for the Arcadia. It needs fumigating, a harbour stamp, a ship's officer's countersignature and a date. Right now it smells of cupboard. <sub>items.adv:140</sub>
- *[if bill_stamped = false]* A Bill of Health, smelling of kelp smoke. Still wants a harbour stamp, and whatever else it wants. <sub>items.adv:142</sub>
- *[if bill_signed = false]* Fumigated and stamped. The line marked SHIP'S OFFICER is empty, and so, possibly, is the date. <sub>items.adv:144</sub>
- *[if bill_dated = false]* Fumigated, stamped, and countersigned “QUILL, NAVIGATOR”. All it lacks is a date, which is what everybody forgets. <sub>items.adv:146</sub>

**calendar leaf** `calendar_leaf` — Today, torn off Pike's calendar. GULLET KEY QUARANTINE STATION. Underneath, in pencil, somebody has written: “Nothing happened.” Not today, it hasn't. <sub>items.adv:149</sub>

**bucket** `bucket` — A bailing bucket off the Arcadia. Empty. It's spent nine years keeping the sea out; it might enjoy carrying some in. <sub>items.adv:152</sub>

**bucket of lagoon** `bucket_water` — A bucket of lagoon, heavier than it looks, and it looks heavy. A small fish has come along for the ride. I'll put him back after. <sub>items.adv:155</sub>

**flag sixteen** `flag16` — Flag number sixteen, made of shirts. One of the patches is a shirt I outgrew when I was twelve. In the corner, in red thread, an L. <sub>items.adv:158</sub>

**Ansel's log** `ansel_log` — My father's log. Six ships, fifteen flags, and one page that isn't to anyone on the sea at all. It's to my mother. <sub>items.adv:161</sub>

**Rook's purse** `purse` — A small leather purse sealed with a wax cloud. Rook's pay for leaving the Arcadia quietly. The seal has never been broken, which is the most honest thing about it. <sub>items.adv:165</sub>

**requisition** `requisition` — A blank Cray & Co. requisition. I've filled it in: one claims book, insurance, all of it. It wants a stamp. Without one it's just handwriting with ambitions. <sub>items.adv:168</sub>

- *[if req_stamped]* REQUISITION: one claims book, insurance, all of it. Authorised: Harbour of Port Vela. Stamped. Nib won't read a word of it, which is the beauty of the thing. <sub>items.adv:170</sub>

**claims book** `claims_book` — Cray & Co.'s insurance claims. Six ships paid in full, for weather. On the facing page, the same year: Captain Vane's storm, refused on a technicality. Somebody underlined it, smugly. <sub>items.adv:173</sub>

**harbour ledger** `ledger` — The harbour ledger, with a length of broken chain still hanging off it. ARCADIA: lost at sea, three days before she was late. Paid, Cray & Co. The page is waiting for a correction. <sub>items.adv:176</sub>

- *[if ledger_written]* ARCADIA: returned. All hands. In my hand, under Bramwick's, stamped. The best entry in the book. <sub>items.adv:178</sub>

**kelp manifest** `kelp_manifest` — QUARANTINE STN, G.K. Briquettes, kelp, four hundred. Purpose, in a careful clerk's hand: for fog. Someone at Cray & Co. writes down exactly what he's told. <sub>items.adv:181</sub>

**manifest copy** `manifest` — The Arcadia's manifest. Twenty-two names, every one marked lost, except one: “R. Rook, navigator. Discharged at sea.” Discharged by whom, in the middle of the sea? <sub>items.adv:184</sub>

<a id="tips"></a>
# Tips

*[the first tip whose condition holds is the one shown (Tip button, H, or tip mode), so within each act they run from the last step back to the first]*

**1.** *[Act I, if has stamped licence and has manifest copy and ledger_read]* You have everything. Give the licence to Bramwick in the customs house. <sub>tips.adv:10</sub>

**2.** *[Act I, if has stamped licence and loft_open and ledger_read = false]* Go up to the loft from Chandler's Lane and open the harbour ledger on the desk. <sub>tips.adv:12</sub>

**3.** *[Act I, if has stamped licence and ledger_read = false]* The harbour ledger is in the loft above the chandler's. Use the crowbar on the bolted shutter in Chandler's Lane. <sub>tips.adv:14</sub>

**4.** *[Act I, if has stamped licence and doesn't have manifest copy]* The chandler keeps manifest copies. Use the harbour stamp on his counter to pay his invoices. <sub>tips.adv:16</sub>

**5.** *[Act I, if has stamped licence]* Show Bramwick your licence: give it to him in the customs house. <sub>tips.adv:18</sub>

**6.** *[Act I, if has harbour stamp and has licence form]* Use the harbour stamp on the licence form. <sub>tips.adv:20</sub>

**7.** *[Act I, if has harbour stamp]* Pick up a blank licence form from Bramwick's desk. <sub>tips.adv:22</sub>

**8.** *[Act I, if has drawer key]* Use the drawer key on Bramwick's drawer in the customs house. <sub>tips.adv:24</sub>

**9.** *[Act I, if has jet-caps and knows_key]* Give the jet-caps to Marta in the Salty Keel. <sub>tips.adv:26</sub>

**10.** *[Act I, if has jet-caps]* Ask Bramwick how a clerk could stamp a licence. Marta wants jet-caps for her broth. <sub>tips.adv:28</sub>

**11.** *[Act I, if knows_key and has crowbar]* Marta wants jet-caps. Use the crowbar on the stacked crate on the pier. <sub>tips.adv:30</sub>

**12.** *[Act I, if knows_key]* Marta wants jet-caps from under the crate on the pier. Pick up the crowbar by the bollard first. <sub>tips.adv:32</sub>

**13.** *[Act I only]* Talk to Bramwick in the customs house (the stone building on the right) about signing on. <sub>tips.adv:34</sub>

**14.** *[Act II, if vane_convinced]* Go forward to the bow (the foredeck, at the back of the main deck) and use the compass on the fog. Call the side the needle swings to. <sub>tips.adv:37</sub>

**15.** *[Act II, if quill_navigator and crew_agree]* Give Pell's log to Captain Vane in her cabin. <sub>tips.adv:39</sub>

**16.** *[Act II, if has Pell's sextant and vane_terms]* Give Pell's sextant to Quill on the main deck. <sub>tips.adv:41</sub>

**17.** *[Act II, if vane_terms and dinner and chest_open = false]* Hobb has gone to dinner. Open Pell's sea-chest below decks. <sub>tips.adv:43</sub>

**18.** *[Act II, if vane_terms and dinner and crew_agree = false]* Give the Arcadia's manifest to Hobb at the mess table below decks. <sub>tips.adv:45</sub>

**19.** *[Act II, if vane_terms and dinner = false]* Go below decks (the hatch on the main deck). Use the harbour stamp on Dorrit's stew. <sub>tips.adv:47</sub>

**20.** *[Act II, if quill_helped]* Go up the quarterdeck steps and down the companionway to the captain's cabin. Use the compass on her chart. <sub>tips.adv:49</sub>

**21.** *[Act II, if has spyglass]* Talk to Quill, ask how to get past, and give her back her spyglass. <sub>tips.adv:51</sub>

**22.** *[Act II, if seen:quill.what]* Quill dropped her spyglass on deck. Look between the crates on the left. <sub>tips.adv:53</sub>

**23.** *[Act II only]* Talk to Quill, the lookout: ask her how to get past to the captain. <sub>tips.adv:55</sub>

**24.** *[Act III, if has flag sixteen]* Cross the reef flats (left of the salt camp) to the wreck, and use flag sixteen on the halyard. <sub>tips.adv:58</sub>

**25.** *[Act III, if quill_free]* Talk to your father, Ansel, in the salt camp. <sub>tips.adv:60</sub>

<a id="ending"></a>
# The Ending

**Closing title:** ALL HANDS RETURNED <sub>acts.adv:37</sub>

- **Title** *[if ending_pirate]* THE PURSER OF THE MARROW <sub>acts.adv:39</sub>
- **Title** *[if ending_desk]* THE HONEST LEDGER <sub>acts.adv:41</sub>
- *[if ending_pirate]* Dawn, from the Marrow's crow's nest. Quill points. “That's the Liar. It moves.” “I'll write it down.” “You do that.” <sub>acts.adv:44</sub>
- *[if ending_pirate and aff ≥ 14]* Her hand is in mine before the Liar has even set. Neither of us writes that down. <sub>acts.adv:46</sub>
- *[if ending_pirate and not aff ≥ 14]* She doesn't hold my hand. She does stand close enough that it would be very easy to. <sub>acts.adv:48</sub>
- *[if ending_pirate]* Flag sixteen flies at the masthead. My mother would have hated the colour. <sub>acts.adv:50</sub>
- *[if ending_desk]* A year later, at the customs-house window: a sail on the horizon, a patchwork flag at her masthead. I stamp her ARRIVED before she's even rounded the light. <sub>acts.adv:53</sub>
- *[if ending_desk and aff ≥ 14]* She comes up the quay at a run, as she does every season, with a new star for me. I've written down four. One of them moves. <sub>acts.adv:55</sub>
- *[if ending_desk and aff ≥ 14 and night_watch]* Every one of them is underlined. <sub>acts.adv:57</sub>
- *[if ending_desk and not aff ≥ 14]* She still calls me cargo. She brings a new star every season, and lets me write it down. <sub>acts.adv:59</sub>
- *[always]* Quill was named navigator of the Marrow. She had it written into the articles, then read out, then read out again. <sub>acts.adv:62</sub>
- *[always]* Captain Vane's storm claim was paid at last, with three years' interest. She uses the letter as a bookmark. <sub>acts.adv:64</sub>
- *[always]* Rook went back to sea, sober. Mostly. On weekdays, and twice on Tuesdays. <sub>acts.adv:66</sub>
- *[if wager and iou_paid]* Bramwick and Marta were married in the spring, paid for by a betting slate and a clerk who backed the right ship. <sub>acts.adv:68</sub>
- *[if wager and iou_paid = false]* My winnings off the betting slate went into a jar behind the Salty Keel's bar, labelled WEDDING, IF HE EVER PAYS UP. It is filling nicely. So, slowly, is his courage. <sub>acts.adv:70</sub>
- *[if iou_paid and wager = false]* Bramwick and Marta are still playing for it, one hand a night. He loses on purpose. She lets him think she can't tell. <sub>acts.adv:72</sub>
- *[if iou_paid = false and wager = false]* Bramwick and Marta are still playing for it, after a fashion. The IOU is in his breast pocket, unpaid, and she has stopped pretending she doesn't know which pocket. <sub>acts.adv:74</sub>
- *[always]* My father opened an instrument shop on the quay. Every compass in it points at Port Vela. He says that isn't a fault; it's a feature, and the feature is home. <sub>acts.adv:76</sub>
- *[if kelp_read]* The last of Cray's kelp went on the Salty Keel's fire. For a week the whole harbour smelled of fog, and laughed. <sub>acts.adv:78</sub>
- *[if kelp_proof and kelp_read = false]* I kept the kelp manifest. FOR FOG. Nobody else ever read it out, and on very clear days I read it to myself. <sub>acts.adv:80</sub>
- *[if silas_refused]* Cray asked for my compass once more, through the bars, very politely. I said no. It runs in the family. <sub>acts.adv:82</sub>
- *[always]* Silas Cray filed an appeal from his cell, in triplicate, as is his right. Nib stamped all three copies without reading them. <sub>acts.adv:84</sub>
- *[always]* ARCADIA: returned. All hands. <sub>acts.adv:86</sub>
